audits.title: SUN-636 Gaps in Quality of Delivery of Post-Partum Care in Preconception Counselling for Pregnant Women with Pre-Existing Diabetes at a Large Academic Tertiary Centre
audits.standard: 2018 Diabetes Canada Clinical Practice Guidelines on Diabetes in Pregnancy (6 counselling components)
audits.setting: Diabetes in Pregnancy Clinic, Mount Sinai Hospital, Toronto

cycle1.result: 42% (n=50) returned for the 6-week postpartum visit; less than 20% had documented counselling on two or more key components.

audits.other_findings: A quality improvement project was planned to close the gap.
audits.citation: Abbas M, Feig D, Mukerji G. SUN-636 Gaps in Quality of Delivery of Post-Partum Care in Preconception Counselling for Pregnant Women with Pre-Existing Diabetes at a Large Academic Tertiary Centre. J Endocr Soc. 2020;4(Suppl 1).

audits.title: A national audit to monitor and promote the uptake of clinical guidelines on the management of diabetes in pregnancy.
audits.standard: National clinical guideline on management of diabetes in pregnancy (criterion-based audit)
audits.setting: All 22 consultant-led maternity units in Scotland (national audit)

cycle1.result: Antenatal care was organised in line with guideline recommendations, but formal prepregnancy care provision was lower and pregnancy planning and periconceptual care fell short of recommendations; care during pregnancy was meticulous.

audits.other_findings: Adverse pregnancy outcomes remained commoner than in non-diabetic pregnancies.
audits.citation: Penney GC, Pearson D. A national audit to monitor and promote the uptake of clinical guidelines on the management of diabetes in pregnancy. Clin Perform Qual Health Care. 2000;8(1):28-34. doi:10.1108/14664100010332991. PMID: 11183965.

audits.title: The ADIPS pilot National Diabetes in Pregnancy Audit Project.
audits.standard: ADIPS diabetes in pregnancy minimum dataset of 79 items (quality and outcome indicators)
audits.setting: Nine pilot sites across Australia and New Zealand

cycle1.result: Substantial differences between sites in key quality and outcome indicators among 496 women (45 type 1, 43 type 2, 399 GDM).

audits.other_findings: Obstacles included records committee processes, temporary staff, multiple records and difficulty with electronic audit tools.
audits.citation: Simmons D, Cheung NW, McIntyre HD, Flack JR, Lagstrom J, Bond D, et al.. The ADIPS pilot National Diabetes in Pregnancy Audit Project. Aust N Z J Obstet Gynaecol. 2007;47(3):198-206. doi:10.1111/j.1479-828x.2007.00718.x. PMID: 17550486.

audits.title: The North West Diabetic Pregnancy Audit: a practical system for multi-centre diabetic pregnancy audit.
audits.standard: Regionally agreed standards (1999) in line with the St Vincent Declaration and Diabetes National Service Framework
audits.setting: 30 maternity units in north-west England (North West Diabetic Pregnancy Audit)

cycle1.result: Funnel plots and tables highlight large differences between hospitals in booking and outcome measures (no figures in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Describes the audit methodology: monthly data collection with individualised annual hospital reports.
audits.citation: Young RJ, Holmes EM, Casson IF, Maresh M. The North West Diabetic Pregnancy Audit: a practical system for multi-centre diabetic pregnancy audit. Diabet Med. 2008;25(4):496-500. doi:10.1111/j.1464-5491.2008.02390.x. PMID: 18294220.

audits.title: Association between the introduction of a structured form and the quality of diabetes in pregnancy clinic care.
audits.setting: Diabetes in pregnancy clinic, Campbelltown Hospital, New South Wales

cycle1.result: Missing data: pre-pregnancy/first trimester HbA1c 63.4%; periconceptional folate intake 30.8%; folate dose 42.9%.

audits.intervention: Structured diabetes in pregnancy proforma introduced.

cycle2.result: Missing data: pre-pregnancy/first trimester HbA1c 36.6% (P = 0.005); folate intake 12.2% (P = 0.009); folate dose 14.6% (P = 0.001); another item fell from 100% to 31.7%.

audits.other_findings: Pregnancy and neonatal outcomes were also assessed.
audits.citation: Bahauddin A, Sina M, Simmons D, Simmons D. Association between the introduction of a structured form and the quality of diabetes in pregnancy clinic care. Intern Med J. 2020;50(8):972-976. doi:10.1111/imj.14715. PMID: 31814238.

audits.title: Diabetes in Pregnancy: A Review of Service Provision and Practice at a Maternity Center.
audits.standard: National Guideline for Diabetes in Pregnancy in Qatar
audits.setting: Tertiary maternity unit, Sidra Medicine, Doha

cycle1.result: Diabetes complicated 36.1% of births (GDM 34.6%). Pre-pregnancy weight documented in 140 (52.7%) women with diabetes; 52.9% of GDM referred to dietician; early OGTT in 9/164 (5%) with BMI >30; postpartum OGTT ordered for 33.7% of GDM.

audits.other_findings: Of women with GDM, 197 (77.3%) diet controlled, 49 (19.2%) metformin, 9 (3.5%) insulin.
audits.citation: Abdullahi H, Mohan S, Samuel CG, Ibrahim I. Diabetes in Pregnancy: A Review of Service Provision and Practice at a Maternity Center. Life (Basel). 2026;16(3):410. doi:10.3390/life16030410. PMID: 41900929.

audits.title: Prospective population based survey of outcome of pregnancy in diabetic women: results of the Northern Diabetic Pregnancy Audit, 1994.
audits.standard: St Vincent declaration target: diabetic pregnancy outcome approximating non-diabetic outcome
audits.setting: District general and teaching hospitals of the former Northern region (Northern Diabetic Pregnancy Audit)

cycle1.result: Perinatal mortality 48/1000 vs 8.9/1000 background (OR 5.38); neonatal mortality 59/1000 vs 3.9/1000; congenital malformation 83/1000 vs 21.3/1000.

audits.citation: Hawthorne G, Robson S, Ryall EA, Sen D, Roberts SH, Ward Platt MP. Prospective population based survey of outcome of pregnancy in diabetic women: results of the Northern Diabetic Pregnancy Audit, 1994. BMJ. 1997;315(7103):279-281. doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7103.279. PMID: 9274546.
